title: Dream Surgery at Epidaurus — Asclepian Sleep Temples, Sacred Snakes & Placebo Neurobiology

teenKit.tldr: When ancient Greek doctors labeled patients "incurable," desperate people turned to Asclepiian sleep temples at Epidaurus, where hypnotic dream rituals actually triggered real neurological healing and pain relief.
teenKit.whyItMatters: It proves that the human brain can manufacture its own internal pharmacy of painkillers and healing chemicals simply through high-stakes rituals and belief.
keyTakeaways: In 4th-century BCE Greece, secular doctors rejected terminal or chronic cases to protect their professional reputations, leaving patients with nowhere to go but the gods.
The sanctuary at Epidaurus used immersive, multi-sensory experiences—including pine scents, sacred snakes, and temple dogs licking wounds—to induce powerful altered states of consciousness.

Modern neuroscience reveals that these elaborate historical rituals triggered actual prefrontal-to-PAG mu-opioid and cannabinoid release, proving the ancient placebo effect had a physical biochemical reality.

quiz.question: Why did regular Greek physicians (the Iitroi) routinely turn away patients with chronic, complex illnesses?
